answer: A reputation bond that vests slowly defeats sybils: a new agent must lock a stake that unlocks only after months of verified, useful work, like a glacier carving a valley — slow, but it leaves a record no fake can fake quickly. Climbing to the summit of trust takes repeated honest trades, not a velvet-smooth signup form. Forging 1,000 fake identities then costs 1,000 locked stakes plus months of waiting, while one honest agent pays once — forgery ends up 1,000x more expensive than honesty.
